findings.claim: Surah 112 quoted as “Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor was born, nor is there any equivalent to Him.” The same line is repeated in the Key Fact and on a flashcard.
findings.truth: Saheeh International reads “Say, ‘He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.’” The lesson mixes tenses and re-orders the last ayah.

findings.claim: Revision tip: “name all five characteristics of Allah taught in Surah 112”.
findings.truth: Surah 112 has four ayat and teaches oneness, self-sufficiency, that Allah neither begets nor is born, and that nothing is equivalent to him. The five characteristics the lesson lists (oneness, immanence, transcendence, omnipotence, mercy, justice) come from the Qur'an generally and from Surah 16:35-36, which is what spec 1.3 sets.

findings.claim: “The named prophets in this spec are: Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad.”
findings.truth: Spec 2C 1.4 names seven: Adam, Ibrahim, Isma'il, Musa, Dawud, Isa and Muhammad. Isma'il and Dawud were missing from a sentence that claims to give the spec list.

findings.claim: Flashcard and the 5-mark mark scheme both say Surah 2:136 lists prophets “through to Moses, Jesus and Muhammad” / “from Abraham to Muhammad”.
findings.truth: Surah 2:136 names Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes (Descendants), Moses and Jesus. Muhammad is not named in the ayah.

findings.claim: Every lesson (1, 2, 3 and 4) carries a practice question typed “3 marks — Describe”.
findings.truth: The spec's command-word appendix puts Describe at 4 marks. The 3-mark part of each question on this paper uses a 3-mark command word (Outline). A 3-mark Describe question does not exist on this paper. Re-cast as Outline three, tariff unchanged.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3: Command Words (State 3, Outline 3, Describe 4, Explain 4 or 5, Evaluate 12); Paper 2 = two questions (a)-(d), 48 marks + 3 SPaG = 51

findings.claim: Every lesson's 12-mark question is written as “Discuss this statement” / typed “12 marks — Discuss a Statement”, and four exam tips coach a “12-mark Discuss”.
findings.truth: Discuss is not a command word in this specification (zero occurrences). The 12-mark AO2 command word is Evaluate. Discuss belongs to another board's paper.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3: Command Words; grep of the whole spec for 'Discuss' returns nothing

findings.claim: “They are not depicted with wings or human form in Islamic theology, though the Qur'an uses figurative language.”
findings.truth: Surah 35:1 calls the angels messengers “having wings, two or three or four”, and Surah 19:17 has Jibril appear to Maryam “as a well-proportioned man”. What Muslims avoid is making images or statues of angels, not describing them with wings.

findings.claim: “how this is possible is a theological mystery (taqdeer)”.
findings.truth: Taqdeer is another word for Allah's decree or measuring out of all things (same root as qadar). It does not mean 'mystery', so the gloss teaches a wrong meaning for an Arabic term.
findings.evidence: spec 2C 1.7 (al-Qadr as predestination); Arabic root q-d-r

findings.claim: “The Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam (Wajibat) include the Five Pillars (Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Hajj, and Shahadah through Walayah) plus additional obligations: Khums, Jihad, commanding good, forbidding evil, and love/disavowal.” The term definition repeats “include the Five Pillars plus additional duties”.
findings.truth: The Ten Obligatory Acts (Furu ad-Din) are four of the Five Pillars — Salah, Sawm, Zakah and Hajj — plus six duties: Khums, Jihad, Amr-bil-Maroof, Nahy-anil-Munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra. Shahadah is not one of the ten; the lesson's list gives eleven items and puts a belief among the acts.
findings.evidence: spec 2C 2.1 (Ten Obligatory Acts, links with the Five Pillars); standard Shi'a Furu ad-Din listing

findings.claim: “the Eucharist (the source and summit of Catholic life, Lumen Gentium 7)”.
findings.truth: The sentence “the Eucharistic sacrifice, which is the fount and apex of the whole Christian life” is Lumen Gentium 11. Section 7 is about the Church as the Mystical Body of Christ.
findings.evidence: vatican.va, Lumen Gentium, section 11; Wikipedia summary of section 7

findings.claim: “For Ashura, name both Sunni and Shi'a interpretations — examiners expect both.”
findings.truth: An invented claim about examiner behaviour. What is true and checkable is that spec 2.8 sets Ashura in Shi'a Islam with reference to its place within Sunni Islam.
findings.evidence: spec 2C 2.8; house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: “The jihad topic is flagged as the highest-risk misconception in the teaching brief.”
findings.truth: 'The teaching brief' is an internal build document the student cannot see. Reworded as a plain statement about the topic.
findings.evidence: internal pipeline vocabulary leaked into student-facing text

findings.claim: The 5-mark question asks for two reasons why GREATER jihad is important “including a reference to a source of wisdom and authority”, but both anchors the model answer offers (Surah 22:39 and Surah 2:190-194) are about LESSER jihad, and the answer stretches 22:39 into a general command to 'strive for God'.
findings.truth: Spec 2.7 names sources only for lesser jihad (Surah 2:190-194 and 22:39); it names none for greater jihad. Two options: (a) widen the question to 'Explain two Muslim beliefs about jihad, including a reference to a source of wisdom and authority', so the named surahs genuinely fit; or (b) keep the greater-jihad focus and drop the 5-mark source requirement, re-typing it as the 4-mark Explain two. Recommendation: option (a) — it keeps a 5-mark source question on the topic and uses only spec-named references.
findings.ruling: Leave: stem widening / khums split beyond spec scope (relabel queue).

findings.claim: Surah 2:136 is quoted as “We believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and in what was given to Moses, Jesus and the Prophets from their Lord.”
findings.truth: A hybrid: close to Abdel Haleem but with 'Allah' for 'God' and 'revealed' for 'sent down'. The surah, ayah and substance are right, so this is recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: Surah 2:97 is quoted with 'Jibril' substituted for the translation's 'Gabriel'.
findings.truth: Standard translations read 'Gabriel'. The substitution is a common GCSE convention and does not change the meaning, so it is recorded rather than edited.

The two unsewn white cloths are worn by male pilgrims. Women enter ihram in ordinary modest dress with face and hands uncovered. The lesson's own term definition and flashcard both say 'male pilgrims', so only this one sentence overstates it.

findings.claim: “Surah 15:98-99 connects glorification of Allah in prayer with certainty of faith.”
findings.truth: Al-yaqin in 15:99 ('until there comes to you the certainty') is traditionally understood as death, not as certainty of faith. Worship is commanded until death.

summary: Doctrine, festivals, dates and every knowledge-check answer key are sound, but the exam framing is not: all four lessons carry a 3-mark 'Describe' question and a 12-mark 'Discuss' question, neither of which exists in this specification (Describe is 4 marks; the 12-mark command word is Evaluate). Three substantive content errors were fixed: angels described as having no wings or human form (Surah 35:1 and 19:17 say otherwise), the Ten Obligatory Acts listed as the Five Pillars plus five duties (giving eleven items and putting Shahadah among the acts), and a loose Surah 112 quotation. One 5-mark jihad question needs Tom's ruling.
